paite: Thugenpa, David tapa, Jerusalem kumpipa thute.
heading: Hinna Phattuamna Bei Ahi
english: The words of the Preacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem:

paite: Bangmah loute bangmah lou, bangmah loute bangmah lou, bang teng bangmah lou ahi, Thugenpa'n achi hi.
english: “Vanity of vanities,” says the Preacher; “Vanity of vanities, all is vanity.”

paite: Asepgimna tengteng ni nuai a asepgim a kipan mihing in bang phattuamna anei a?
english: What does man gain from all his labor in which he labors under the sun?

paite: Khang khat apai a, khang dang ahong tung a; tangtawn in lei a-om gige.
english: One generation goes, and another generation comes; but the earth remains forever.

paite: Ni leng asuak zel a, ni atum zel; huchi in asuahna mun lam ah akik nawn pah hi.
english: The sun also rises, and the sun goes down, and hurries to its place where it rises.

paite: Simlam ah huih apai a, mallam ah akilehhei a; alampi ah akivialhei gige, huan huih alam zuih ah akik nawn zel hi.
english: The wind goes toward the south, and turns around to the north. It turns around continually as it goes, and the wind returns again to its courses.

paite: Luite tengteng tuipi ah aluanglut ua, himahleh tuipi a dim tuan kei; luite paina mun lam ah, huai lam ah apai nawn uh.
english: All the rivers run into the sea, yet the sea is not full. To the place where the rivers flow, there they flow again.

paite: Thil tengteng gimna in adim a; mihing in agen thei kei; muh in mit alungkim kei a, zak in bil leng alungkim sam kei.
english: All things are full of weariness beyond uttering. The eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear filled with hearing.

paite: A-om khinsa ahong om ding ahi a; hih khitsa hih a om ding ahi a; huchi in ni nuai ah thil thak a-om kei hi.
english: That which has been is that which shall be, and that which has been done is that which shall be done; and there is no new thing under the sun.

paite: En dih, "Hiai athak ahi?" chi a mite'n agen uh thil a-om hia? I ma ua hunte ua a-om khinsa ahi.
english: Is there a thing of which it may be said, “Behold, this is new”? It has been long ago, in the ages which were before us.

paite: Khang masate theihgigena a-om kei a; anung a hong om dingte lak ah hong om ding khang nanung lam theihgigena leng a-om sam kei ding.
english: There is no memory of the former; neither shall there be any memory of the latter that are to come, among those that shall come after.

paite: Kei Thugenpa, Jerusalem ah Israel tung a kumpipa ka hi.
heading: Mipil Tuahsate A Kipan A Thil Theih
english: I, the Preacher, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.

paite: Van nuai a hih a omte tengteng tungtang pilna a zong ding leh zongkhe ding a ka lungtang suah ka hi; huai a kisuk ding a mite tapate kiang a Pathian in apiak nakpitak a gimna ahi.
english: I applied my heart to seek and to search out by wisdom concerning all that is done under the sky. It is a heavy burden that God has given to the sons of men to be afflicted with.

paite: Ni nuai a hih a om nasepte tengteng ka muta a; ngai in, bang teng bangmah lou ahi a, huih nungdelh ahi.
english: I have seen all the works that are done under the sun; and behold, all is vanity and a chasing after wind.

paite: Akawisa bawl tang theih ahi kei; huan akim lou sim theih ahi kei.
english: That which is crooked can’t be made straight; and that which is lacking can’t be counted.

paite: Keimah lungtang ka houlimpih a, "Ngai in, Jerusalem a ka ma a omte tengteng sang in pilna thupi ka hon muhsak a; ahi, ka lungtang in pilna aneita," chi in.
english: I said to myself, “Behold, I have obtained for myself great wisdom above all who were before me in Jerusalem. Yes, my heart has had great experience of wisdom and knowledge.”

paite: Huchi in pilna thei ding leh haina haitatna thei ding in ka lungtang ka suk a; hiai leng huih nungdelh ahi chih ka thei hi.
english: I applied my heart to know wisdom, and to know madness and folly. I perceived that this also was a chasing after wind.

paite: Pil mahmahna ah lungkham mahmahna a-om a; kuapeuh theihna khangsak in lungkhamna akhangsak hi.
english: For in much wisdom is much grief; and he who increases knowledge increases sorrow.
